1.pericope_label: And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book. And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.

schools.summary: Place the trouble in the period before the hostile king's overthrow, press the wording many where all was expected, and keep Michael an angelic helper whose presence supports rather than averts.
Identify Michael with the Son of God and read the resurrection literally, joining the church's preservation to the second coming because no source of salvation is found on earth.
Divide on the identification, one taking the archangel as the reputed guardian of the Jewish people, the other making him the Messiah appearing for their salvation.
Reads the passage as the prophets' usual practice of furnishing an antidote with the malady, no relief being so sovereign as one fetched from Christ and the future state.

positions.position: The Son of God, the name meaning one who is as God, standing up in a spiritual presence among his people rather than at the incarnation or the last appearing.
The great prince who stands when persecution is hottest and stood for his people when made a curse for them.
The Messiah appearing for their salvation, the phrase at that time covering the whole space between the two comings.
The archangel, ever reputed the guardian of the Jewish people.
A helper whose presence does not avert the times of trouble but supports God's people through them.

debates.question: Is the awakening of the sleepers literal or figurative?

positions.position: Literal, the resurrection of the dead at the last day; the figurative readings of a Jewish commentator, a heathen critic and some Christian writers are rejected.
Both: referred to a future restoration of the Jews and true also at the general judgment.
A general resurrection, with many implying a contrast to the few alive and remaining rather than standing for all.
The angel joins the salvation of the church to the final resurrection because no source of salvation is met with on earth.

outliers.claim: Fixes the time of distress as the climax of the hostile king's oppression, falling at the expiry of the last week, and traces the description to an earlier prophet with the superlative clause heightened from elsewhere.

themes: And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.
And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.

3.pericope_label: And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever. But thou, O Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end: many shall run to and fro, and knowledge shall be increased.

schools.summary: Keep the wise inside the book, referring them back to the previous chapter and defining their wisdom as covenant faithfulness or as instruction that strengthened others under tribulation.
Weigh whether the participle is transitive and turn the sealing into a question about the obscurity of prophecy.
Read the wise as those instructed in Christ's doctrine, and state the rule that only prophecies long in fulfilling were ordered to be sealed.

debates.question: Who are the wise that shall shine?

positions.position: The spiritually wise, wise unto salvation, who shine in body and soul at the resurrection.
Those instructed in Christ's word, distinguished by holiness of life and purity of creed.
Not teachers only but the intelligent who awakened their contemporaries to fidelity, some sealing their testimony in war with their blood.
The same as those who understand in the previous chapter, their wisdom being covenant faithfulness that set a bright example.
Those endued with intellect, the word probably transitive here since the office of justifying is presently assigned to them.

debates.question: What is meant by running to and fro?

positions.position: Many searching out the sense, knowledge increasing by that means though the meaning waits on the events.
The verb is used elsewhere of searching after knowledge and of the eyes of the Lord ranging the earth.
Searching the prophecies and knowing the signs of the times, chiefly in gospel times.
Not the received sense that few would be worthy to receive it; there is no cause for despondency because few receive it, the prophecy remaining a precious treasure though despised.

outliers.claim: Adds an antiquarian note on sealing: among the ancients those were said to seal who in reading stamped the places of which they were doubtful, to keep them in memory and return to them.

themes: And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.
But thou, O Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end: many shall run to and fro, and knowledge shall be increased.

5.pericope_label: Then I Daniel looked, and, behold, there stood other two, the one on this side of the bank of the river, and the other on that side of the bank of the river. And one said to the man clothed in linen, which was upon the waters of the river, How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?

schools.summary: Explain why the revelation does not end at the sealing, and reason from the absent article that the two figures had not been seen before.
Make the prophet's calm attentiveness the ground of the vision's credibility, and take the man in linen for Christ.
Say only that they are probably two angels and that the man in linen is Gabriel in human form.
Reduces the close of the book to two questions, when the end shall be and what the end shall be.

debates.question: Who is the man clothed in linen?

positions.position: Christ in human form, a presage of the incarnation, the linen expressing the priestly office and the purity that qualified him for it.
Gabriel in human form, as in an earlier chapter.
The person of the earlier chapter, pointed out by the article and the clothing, and not now first coming into view.

debates.question: Who asks how long it shall be?

positions.position: Evidently one of the two just mentioned, though the Greek version and a Latin father suppose the prophet himself.
Which angel spoke is not said; very probably each spoke in turn and joined in the same request.

outliers.claim: Makes the man's position over the waters symbolic: if streams are emblems of nationalities, the river represents the Persian empire and the hovering implies power over it.
Grounds the vision's credibility in the prophet's own attentiveness, since the narrative would not have produced confidence had he not applied his mind seriously to these mysteries.

themes: Then I Daniel looked, and, behold, there stood other two, the one on this side of the bank of the river, and the other on that side of the bank of the river.
And one said to the man clothed in linen, which was upon the waters of the river, How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?

7.pericope_label: And I heard the man clothed in linen, which was upon the waters of the river, when he held up his right hand and his left hand unto heaven, and sware by him that liveth for ever that it shall be for a time, times, and an half; and when he shall have accomplished to scatter the power of the holy people, all these things shall be finished. And I heard, but I understood not: then said I, O my Lord, what shall be the end of these things? And he said, Go thy way, Daniel: for the words are closed up and sealed till the time of the end.

schools.summary: State the ordinary rule of swearing with one hand, rule out any reference to the Greek persecution on the ground of the measures of time, and read the dismissal as a refusal that is not wholly a refusal.
Correct those who take the raised hands for a symbol of power, and make the prophet's confession of not understanding a credential of his diligence.
Resolve the period into years and their prophetic equivalents, one of them venturing a date for the time of the end.

debates.question: What is the time, times and a half?

positions.position: A year, two years and half a year, with the equivalents of forty-two months and twelve hundred and sixty days.
Prophetic time answering to twelve hundred and sixty years.
Whatever it is, any reference to the persecution under the Greek king is impossible, given the difference between the measures of time.
Quieting and at once a refusal to answer, yet not wholly a refusal, since the end is not so revealed that men can know it beforehand.
Be at peace: nothing further is explained, and the prophet is only assured the end will come.
Either attend to the affairs of the court, or write the visions for posterity, or go the way of all flesh.
The wish was pious and lawful, but God did not grant it, wishing some predictions partially understood and the rest concealed.

outliers.claim: Ventures a calculation from the sealed words and predicts that the time of the end will not arrive before the twentieth century.

themes: And I heard the man clothed in linen, which was upon the waters of the river, when he held up his right hand and his left hand unto heaven, and sware by him that liveth for ever that it shall be for a time, times, and an half; and when he shall have accomplished to scatter the power of the holy people, all these things shall be finished.
And I heard, but I understood not: then said I, O my Lord, what shall be the end of these things?
And he said, Go thy way, Daniel: for the words are closed up and sealed till the time of the end.

10.pericope_label: Many shall be purified, and made white, and tried; but the wicked shall do wickedly: and none of the wicked shall understand; but the wise shall understand. And from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days. Blessed is he that waiteth, and cometh to the thousand three hundred and five and thirty days.

schools.summary: Divide sharply over the numbered days, one referring the abomination to the Greek desecration and the other calling the relation of the periods an apparently insoluble difficulty.
Read the purification as the answer given in place of the one asked for, and deny that the passage can refer to the Greek profanation at all.
Make the abomination a proverbial phrase applicable to anything set against God's ordinances, and compute the longer period as years.

debates.question: To what does the taking away of the daily sacrifice refer?

positions.position: To the desecration under the Greek king, since the words point back so distinctly to the previous chapter.
Not to that profanation at all; the angel witnesses to a destruction so complete as to leave no hope of restoration.
The phrase is proverbial and fits anything substituted for the ordinances of God, such as a pagan temple on the temple site or a church turned into a mosque.
The doctrine of atonement by the sacrifice of Christ, taken away by antichrist when the doctrine of works was established.
The same subject as the previous chapter, the language about the abomination being almost verbally identical with three earlier passages.

outliers.claim: Names the crux without solving it, calling the relation of the two longer numbers to the twenty-three hundred days and to the time, times and a half a great and apparently insoluble difficulty.
Supplies the pastoral motive for announcing the persecutions, that our minds fall down lifeless through terror before it comes to blows, so our imbecility requires many stimulants to patience.

themes: Many shall be purified, and made white, and tried; but the wicked shall do wickedly: and none of the wicked shall understand; but the wise shall understand.
And from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days.
Blessed is he that waiteth, and cometh to the thousand three hundred and five and thirty days.

13.pericope_label: But go thou thy way till the end be: for thou shalt rest, and stand in thy lot at the end of the days.

schools.summary: Finds the figure behind the word lot in the partition of Palestine by lot, one greater than Joshua dividing the heavenly Canaan among the saints.
Reads the two verbs as announcement rather than command, thou shalt rest meaning thou shalt die and thou shalt stand meaning death is not complete destruction.
Turn the last verse outward to the reader, one in four heads of advice and the other in a rule about securing a happy lot.

debates.question: How is the closing command to be taken?

positions.position: Prepare for death and expect to lie in the grave until the resurrection morning.
Not a command but an announcement of what will happen, God causing him to stand in his lot with the rest of the elect after the church has been humbled and purged.
Four heads of advice addressed to every reader: walk in thy assigned way, be faithful unto death, expect rest for body and soul, and stand in thine own lot.
The revelation was given so that prophet and people might be prepared for sufferings yet not without hope of a glorious deliverance.

outliers.claim: Takes the lot as an allusion to the partition of the land by lot under Joshua, so that one greater than Joshua divides the heavenly Canaan among those who follow this prophet in faith and firmness.

themes: But go thou thy way till the end be: for thou shalt rest, and stand in thy lot at the end of the days.
